meta_title: MeteoRide — the weather on your route, stretch by stretch
meta_description: Load a GPX or KML route and see rain, wind and temperature for every stretch at the hour you ride through it. Free, no account, no ads. iPhone, Android and web.
hero_title: The weather on your route, at the hour you ride through it
hero_pitch: Load a GPX or KML route, set your start time and speed, and MeteoRide shows rain, wind and temperature for every stretch at the time you will be there.
store_badge_label: Download MeteoRide on the App Store
alt_hero_desktop: MeteoRide on a laptop: a route on the map and the weather table for each stretch
alt_hero_phone: MeteoRide on a phone: the weather table for a route
card1_text: Temperature, wind and gusts, rain and its probability, humidity, cloud and UV for each point, at the hour you pass it.
card2_text: Wind arrows and rain droplets along the route. Tap a column of the table and the map centres on that point.
card3_text: The warnings of national weather services that overlap your ride, through OpenWeather with your own key.
card4_text: The app keeps watching the route and tells you if rain, wind or strong gusts, or an official warning appear for the hours you will be out.
card5_text: Prepare the route at home with 📴: the route and its table are still there when you lose coverage.
card6_text: Providers side by side over the same route, or two start times to pick when to leave.
card7_text: Receive a GPX from Komoot, Strava or Files, and send it on to your head unit, Files or mail.
card8_text: Optional userscripts add a button on Komoot, Bikemap and Hammerhead that opens the route in MeteoRide.
block_a_title: Every stretch, at the hour you get there
block_a_text: Each column is a point on the route: time and distance, temperature, wind with gusts, rain in mm/h with its probability, humidity, cloud and UV. Sunrise, sunset and civil twilight are marked, and a bar shows the light in each interval.
alt_table: The weather table on a laptop: one column per point of the route
block_b_text: Wind arrows coloured by strength and droplets where rain is expected, over the route itself, with its start and finish marked.
alt_map: The route map on a phone, with wind arrows and rain droplets
block_c_text: Open-Meteo, global and up to 14 days ahead, is the default. AROME-HD from Météo-France gives high resolution over France and nearby countries for 36 hours. OpenWeather works with your own key. Choose Compare to see them together, or press ⇄ and then ⟲ to compare two start times.
alt_compare: Compare mode on a laptop: several providers for the same route
block_d_title: Warnings, and a heads-up if it changes
block_d_text: With an OpenWeather key, the official warnings that overlap your ride appear with the route. The app keeps watching it and sends you a notification like this one if the weather turns worse.
alt_warning: An official weather warning shown in the app on a phone

step3_text: A table and a map with the forecast along the route, every 15 or 30 minutes.

android_text: Install the APK from GitHub. Android 7 or later. Coming to Google Play.
web_text: Nothing to install: open it in your browser. You can add it to your home screen like an app.
privacy_1: No account, no sign-up, no ads, no analytics, no tracking.
privacy_2: Your settings and recent routes are stored on your device.
privacy_3: Open source under the MIT licence: anyone can check what it does.
faq1_a: Yes. MeteoRide is free, with no account and no ads.
faq2_q: Do I need an API key?
faq2_a: No. Open-Meteo and AROME-HD work without one. Only OpenWeather, and the official warnings that come from it, need your own key, which you enter in Settings.
faq3_q: Does it work out of signal?
faq3_a: In the app, if you prepare it: press 📴 at home and the route keeps its forecast. Opening the app brings back the last route with its table, and a forecast up to twelve hours old is still shown, labelled with its age. The map background needs a connection and may be blank.
faq4_a: As accurate as the forecast it comes from: MeteoRide shows what the providers forecast, it does not make its own. From day 3 or 4 onwards forecasts are markedly less reliable. Compare sources when the decision matters, and check your official weather service before a ride that could be affected.
faq5_q: Does it work with Garmin or Karoo?
faq5_a: MeteoRide runs on your phone or computer, not on the head unit. The app shares the route as a GPX with any app that accepts it, such as your head unit's. On the web, an optional userscript sends it to the Hammerhead dashboard.
faq6_a: There is no account. Your settings, routes and key are kept on your device. To compute the forecast, the route's points go to the weather providers, and the map is loaded from OpenStreetMap; the privacy policy lists exactly what each one receives.
